parts.text:
29 Light of wavelength 567 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating. The grating has
400 lines per mm. A number of diffraction maxima are observed on the far side of the grating.
What is the angle between the second-order maximum and the third-order maximum?
A
13.1°
B
13.9°
C
15.9°
D
27.0°

hints: Convert the 400 lines per mm specification into the slit spacing $d$ in metres: $d = 10^{-3}/400 = 2.50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and convert 567 nm to $567 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
Recall the normal-incidence grating condition $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ and apply it separately for order $n=2$ and order $n=3$ to get $\sin\theta_2$ and $\sin\theta_3$.
Find $\theta_2 = \sin^{-1}(2\lambda/d)$ and $\theta_3 = \sin^{-1}(3\lambda/d)$ in degrees, then subtract $\theta_3 - \theta_2$ - do not stop at a single order angle.
walkthrough: Find the grating spacing from 400 lines per mm: $d = \frac{1.00 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}}{400} = 2.50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
State the diffraction grating equation for normal incidence: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, with $\lambda = 567 \text{ nm} = 567 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.

The question asks for the angle between these two diffracted beams on the same side, so subtract: $\Delta\theta = \theta_3 - \theta_2 \approx 42.9^{\circ} - 27.0^{\circ} \approx 15.9^{\circ}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $\theta_1$ for $n=1$, since $\sin\theta_1 = 567 \times 10^{-9} / 2.50 \times 10^{-6}$, giving about $13.1^{\circ}$ from the zero order, not the gap between $n=2$ and $n=3$.

B.explanation: This is approximately $\theta_2 - \theta_1 \approx 27.0^{\circ} - 13.1^{\circ}$, the gap between the first- and second-order maxima, not between the second and third.

C.explanation: The difference $\theta_3 - \theta_2 \approx 42.9^{\circ} - 27.0^{\circ} \approx 15.9^{\circ}$ follows from $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ for $n=2$ and $n=3$.

D.explanation: This is $\theta_2$ alone for $n=2$, since $\sin\theta_2 = 2 \times 567 \times 10^{-9} / 2.50 \times 10^{-6}$, not the difference $\theta_3 - \theta_2$.
